🧭 Product
Navigation Update · Live

Timesheets — View Summary Navigation

Payroll Summary is now a first-class navigable page from Timesheets Pay Period view. The old Download Timesheets modal is removed, and the right entry point now depends on account type.

▶ Watch Timesheets View Summary Loom
🧭
What sales needs to know: OAMs now get a clearer path to Payroll Summary from Timesheets → Pay Period view. The summary opens as a dedicated page instead of being buried inside a download utility flow.
👥
Entry point depends on account type: Non-payroll OAMs use View summary; Homebase Payroll OAMs keep Run payroll primary and find View summary plus Download time cards in Tools; Clover OAMs use Send to ADP, which now opens the summary page.
🧾
What changed on the page: Payroll Summary now has a pay-period date picker and a breadcrumb back to Timesheets. Download time cards regenerates the totals cache so the CSV is current.
🚫
What did not change: No changes for non-OAM roles, and the summary page content, columns, and provider export buttons remain unchanged.
Rep direction: For “where did summary go?” or “how do I download timesheets?” questions, route customers to Timesheets → Pay Period view → View summary. Payroll customers: Tools → View summary. Time-card CSV: Tools → Download time cards.
⚙️ CS Ops
Functionality Update · June 22

Active Payroll Companies Can’t Be Archived Until Payroll Is Canceled

ActiveAdmin now prevents company archival when an active Payroll subscription still exists. This keeps Payroll subscriptions from landing in a bad state after archive.

✅
What sales needs to know: Teams will no longer be able to archive a company in ActiveAdmin while that company still has an active Payroll subscription.
🛡️
Why it’s changing: Archiving active Payroll companies can put the payroll subscription into a bad state. This adds a guardrail before that can happen.
➡️
How it impacts day-to-day: If a customer needs an account archived, make sure Payroll is canceled first. Archive comes after Payroll cancellation, not before.
Small but important process note: This is primarily a CS/Admin guardrail. No customer notification is planned.
Functionality Update

Terminated Employees No Longer Trigger PTO Request Notifications

Managers should stop receiving email, SMS, push, or in-app notifications for time-off requests from terminated employees. Stale requests are also removed from the Requests Feed inbox where applicable.

🔕
What sales needs to know: Time-off requests from terminated employees should no longer create manager notifications across email, SMS, push, or in-app alerts.
🧹
Why it’s changing: This cleans up stale PTO noise and prevents managers from being pulled into requests from people who are no longer active.
💬
How it impacts day-to-day: If a customer asks why those PTO notifications stopped appearing, this is expected behavior — not a notification bug.
📣 PMM
Competitive Watch

Payroll Promo Watch: Competitors Are Moving Toward 6-Month Offers

PMM is seeing several payroll competitors shift into longer free-period offers. Treat this as a positioning watch-out, not a change to the approved Homebase offer.

Competitive payroll offers in market as of 6/12/2026
📌
What sales needs to know: The market is getting more aggressive on headline payroll promos, with some competitors showing 6-month free offers or deeper bundled discounts.
🔎
Why it matters: Homebase’s approved offer still gives reps a clear promo hook, but discount length may become less differentiated as more competitors extend their offers.
💬
How it impacts day-to-day: Don’t get stuck comparing month counts. Anchor back to the full Homebase value story: Payroll plus scheduling, time tracking, team management, switching support, and fewer disconnected systems.
Important: Do not promise a six-month match or any non-standard promo unless PMM / RevOps publishes an approved offer.
